title: NBA League Pass Rankings, Part 5
contentHtml:
Well, everyone, we made it—to the top six of these League Pass Rankings, and to opening night of a much-anticipated NBA season. Thanks to everyone who has checked in, dabbled, and subscribed. It has been fun to discover my fingers still work, and with this annual tradition fulfilled—for the 13th time!—I’m looking forward to a new season and to getting this newsletter into what will be its normal weekly rhythm.

You know what I’m also looking forward to? Watching the six teams featured below. They bring some of the meatiest subplots, thorniest lineup questions, and biggest stars. They all enter facing varying degrees and types of franchise-warping pressure.

So without further ado, the top six. Do we have a new no. 1? A repeat winner? Any plot twists? Dive in—and buckle up for the season!

Subscribe now

6. Los Angeles Lakers (38.5)

Luka Doncic with a real rim runner, shooting everywhere, and one capable secondary ball handler—Austin Reaves, maybe the best first-time All-Star bet—is a must-watch chess game. It unfolds slowly enough that you can process it in real time—Doncic digesting each new coverage, downloading all possible counters, choosing the meanest one, and then twisting the knife with shoulder shakes, calculated glances, pass fakes, and funky pivots. He puts the whole defense in hell and then dangles it over the edge of an inferno for brief seconds that must feel like forever.

He has every pass and knows how to open lanes for all of them. He creates lobs when they really shouldn’t be there by staring down his corner shooter—a decoy—or rising for a floater that turns into an alley-oop once the defender bites. Perhaps the best, and cruelest, of all of Doncic’s tricks: when he picks up his dribble under the rim and unleashes a ball fake so convincing the defender literally turns his head in the wrong direction, only for Doncic to throw some blind wrap-around or overhead lob.

It all crescendos into glaring, cutting trash talk—the best kind. The flip side: Doncic’s endless complaining to the officials gets tiresome. And while it’s massively helpful to winning, the Lakers leading the league in free throws every year slices away at their overall watchability—and not because there is any conspiracy to help the Lakers (there isn’t). Stoppages are boring. That said, I did not enjoy the “one free throw for all the points” experiment in summer league. It feels too gimmicky. Just enforce the 10-second clock (what’s up, Giannis!) and streamline the process.

Walker Kessler is an enigma after missing almost all of last season and playing zero meaningful games in Utah. I expect a big year from him; he might lead the league in offensive rebounds and putbacks. He’ll have to clean up a lot of messes on defense, though JJ Redick and his staff are as inventive as it gets there; the Lakers always seem to outperform their talent on that end.

Redick is good for at least two instantly memeable rage timeouts per season, though he can no longer direct his ire at Dalton Knecht for forgetting plays; the Lakers waived Knecht on Monday. Gulp. (Remember those two weeks when the Lakers were hailed as geniuses for “stealing” Knecht at no. 17? It was an entire media cycle! That was fun. Redraft today, and at least eight of the 13 guys taken after Knecht in the first round in 2024 would go before him.)

Bookmark approximately November 15 for the first “Can Jarred Vanderbilt shoot corner 3s now?” news cycle—and then November 22 for that cycle to end with “still no.”

Ziaire Williams and Matisse Thybulle are worthy reclamation projects—Thybulle was awesome in limited action last season—and if one even kind of hits, it could change the Lakers’ season. Thybulle is a phantasmic playmaker on defense—teleporting across huge spaces to muck things up.

I’m a sucker for Bronny James maybe leaping from his dad’s shadow. Jaden Hardy has spunk to his game on offense. Collin Sexton plays with reckless, head-down aggression and the bravado of someone who thinks—really thinks—he is the best player on the floor at all times. He should do damage on second units alongside either Doncic or Reaves.

The Lakers have the league’s best floor and one of the three or four best jersey sets. Even the white alternates have grown on me. The endless ownership drama gets them zero points here, unless it spills onto the floor in some Buss sibling brawl.
